presenceLabel: Mingo town, camp or raid site in this area
presenceNote: Presence only, no mapped boundary. The years 1770 to 1776 are the dated sources (Washington at Mingo Town 1770; Yellow Creek 1774; the Georgetown raid Dec 1776); No dated source supports an earlier start. No source locates a Mingo camp in Kentucky, so no area and no Kentucky camp is drawn. “Mingo” is an outsiders’ name.
overlapNote: Mingo were the Six Nations’ resident presence in Ohio and were named as parties ("Mingoes of Ohio") in the Fort Stanwix deed and attended the treaty, so this page relates directly to six-nations.json. The same small hunting camps were used by Shawnee, Delaware, Cherokee and Tutelo in the mid-1700s (Henderson 1992). Kentucky was also claimed by the Shawnee and Cherokee.
basis: Henderson 1992 (general statement), Washington’s 1770 diary (Mingo Town), Wikipedia for the Yellow Creek massacre and Pluggy, NPS/USFS for the 1776 raids. No Mingo area is drawn. Native Land Digital data was not used.

legend.label: Approximate general area of Mingo presence on the upper Ohio (whole counties, not a boundary)

eras.label: 1770–1774 · Mingo Town, Ohio
eras.text: Mingo of Ohio attended the 1768 Fort Stanwix treaty, which ceded the land south of the Ohio to the Crown. In Oct 1770 Washington found about 20 cabins and 70 people at Mingo Town on the Ohio (Jefferson Co., Ohio; point approximate). The tint is an approximate general area of Mingo presence on the upper Ohio, built from whole counties. Henderson (1992) says small Mingo, Shawnee and other hunting camps existed south of the river in the mid-1700s and later moved north; no source gives where any Kentucky camp was, so none is drawn.

eras.label: 1774–1776 · Yellow Creek and Dunmore’s War
eras.text: Logan lived at Yellow Creek on the upper Ohio, where Virginians killed his relatives on 30 Apr 1774, leading into Dunmore’s War. The point is approximate (near the site, on the West Virginia bank), inside the tinted general area of Mingo presence on the upper Ohio. Henderson says hunting parties became raiding parties in the 1770s.

notDrawn.map: MINGO CAMPS IN KENTUCKY: SITES UNKNOWN · NOT DRAWN

eras.label: 1776 · Raid on McClelland’s Station (Kentucky)
eras.text: On 25 Dec 1776 the Mingo chief Pluggy attacked Harrod’s Town, and on 29 Dec he attacked McClelland’s Station at Georgetown and was killed. The raiders came from the Ohio country (the tinted upper-Ohio area is the general area of Mingo presence; Pluggy’s own town is not located). The Georgetown point marks a RAID, not a camp, and is approximate.

properties.label: Mingo Town (1770)
properties.name: Mingo Town, Jefferson Co. OH (1770, approximate)
properties.note: Mingo Town (Shenanjee), west bank of the Ohio a little above the Cross Creeks, Jefferson Co., Ohio: about 20 cabins and 70 Six Nations inhabitants on 22 Oct 1770 (Washington). Point is the modern Mingo Junction village (40.321, -80.609), which the editors of Washington’s papers place near the old town (Cross Creeks about 3¼ miles below Steubenville). Approximate to a few miles.

properties.label: Yellow Creek (1774)
properties.name: Yellow Creek mouth / massacre area, 1774 (approximate)
properties.note: Yellow Creek massacre, 30 Apr 1774: on the West Virginia bank across from the mouth of Yellow Creek; Logan lived at the creek mouth (Ohio side). Point is the Mountaineer Casino location given by Wikipedia as near the site. Approximate to a few miles.

properties.label: McClelland’s Station RAID, 29 Dec 1776 (a raid, not a camp)
properties.name: McClelland’s Station raid, Georgetown KY, 29 Dec 1776 (approximate)
properties.note: McClelland’s Station, Georgetown, Scott Co.: Pluggy’s Mingo raid of 29 Dec 1776 (Pluggy killed). A raid, not a camp. Point is the Georgetown town centre from Wikipedia; the station site itself is not located to better than the town.
Main-map extent: general areas (whole-county shapes, approximate), solid lines in Kentucky and sourced points.

Upper Ohio valley around Mingo Town (Jefferson Co., Ohio) and Yellow Creek, from the 1770 diary and the Yellow Creek account; Pluggy's Town (north of Columbus) is not located and not included. Counties are used only to give a generous general area; the edge follows county lines and is not a boundary.
